subject.title: [Feature]: Capture reusable techniques from successful agent work

question: Should autonomous Skill Workshop infer reusable techniques from successful trajectories without an explicit correction or `/learn` request, and should that reflection delay the final reply?
rationale: The request changes agent initiative, turn latency, and the evidence threshold for durable learned behavior; source inspection cannot safely choose those product semantics.

options.title: Add gated successful-run reflection
options.body: Use the existing opt-in and pending-review boundary with strict success, nontriviality, reuse, evidence, secret, and no-op gates before the final reply.

options.title: Keep explicit learning triggers
options.body: Continue requiring prospective instructions, corrections, or `/learn` to avoid speculative proposals and extra turn latency.

options.title: Evaluate asynchronous reflection
options.body: Run reflection after delivery and surface proposals later, trading immediate visibility for lower reply latency.

recommendation.title: Add gated successful-run reflection
recommendation.body: Use the existing opt-in and pending-review boundary with strict success, nontriviality, reuse, evidence, secret, and no-op gates before the final reply.

likelyOwner.reason: He opened the narrowed proposal and has recent history on the current agent-end Skill Research integration, making him the strongest available owner for its intended autonomy semantics.
